history.summary: A historical Shaktipeeth at Banbhori village; tradition holds the temple ~400 years old and the idol self-manifested (swoyambhu) from the earth - oral tradition only, no dated epigraphic record found. Legend: the goddess Bhramari manifested as a swarm of bees (bhramara) to kill the demon Arunasura, who was disturbing the penance of sages. A 24-hour Akhand Jyoti burns in the sanctum. The temple was privately served by a Brahmin family until the Haryana cabinet brought it under the government-run Shri Durga Mata Mandir Banbhori Temple Trust in November 2017. Fairs twice a year during Navratri draw lakhs of devotees. Town corrected: CSV says 'Hisar' but the temple is at Banbhori village (Barwala tehsil, Hisar district), ~55 km NE of Hisar city. Coordinates approximate (village-level).

name: Maa Bhanbhori Bhramri Devi Temple
town_description: Banbhori (also spelt Banbhauri) is a village in Barwala tehsil of Hisar district, Haryana, on the Hisar-Barwala-Banbhori-Uchana road. It is a small rural settlement whose fame rests almost entirely on the Shri Durga Mata Bhramari Mandir, a Shaktipeeth that draws large pilgrim crowds during Navratri fairs. The village economy is agricultural, supplemented by temple-related trade.
